card: Adds a TxCollection mining IPC interface that allows external services, like Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers (JDS), to assemble and validate candidate block templates from a list of WTXIDs without maintaining duplicate mempool mirrors. External template coordinators currently synchronize duplicate mempools by repeatedly polling complete templates over IPC, incurring substantial bandwidth and memory overhead. The interface resolves WTXIDs against the local mempool, ingests missing raw transactions, and validates the assembled block against the chain tip using TestBlockValidity with an optional caller-supplied coinbase. The change enables downstream Stratum v2 JDS support demonstrated in sv2-apps PR #599.
changed_since_previous: Rebased onto recent changes (such as the merged block template manager); core architecture and features remain unchanged.
evidence: PR description notes that Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers currently must maintain 'its own mempool mirror, which it populates by repeatedly calling getBlock() and waitNext() and then requesting any missing transactions from the miner', which this PR removes.
The new interface is already integrated and demonstrated in Stratum v2 reference tooling via stratum-mining/sv2-apps PR #599.
problem: External mining coordinators that validate and approve miner-selected block templates (such as Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers) currently maintain duplicate out-of-process mempool mirrors. Keeping those mirrors synchronized requires repeatedly fetching entire block templates or pulling missing transactions over IPC, creating significant memory and bandwidth overhead.

risk.why: Flaws in block template assembly or validation could cause mining coordinators to approve invalid candidate blocks or crash IPC server processes.

scope_notes: Adds node::TxCollection and implements its IPC bindings; extracts BlockAssembler::CreateCoinbaseTx() from miner.cpp without changing existing block template creation behavior.
summary: Adds a TxCollection interface to Bitcoin Core's mining subsystem and Cap'n Proto IPC interface to allow external clients to reconstruct and validate block templates from an ordered list of witness transaction IDs (WTXIDs). The interface identifies which transactions are absent from the node's mempool, accepts missing transaction payloads from the caller, and assembles candidate block templates validated against the active chain tip via TestBlockValidity. It also refactors coinbase generation in BlockAssembler into a standalone helper to support both node-generated dummy coinbases and custom caller-provided coinbases.
